title: Forward/reverse conveyor
summary: Return conveyor CV-7: forward and reverse with electrical interlocks, one overload and a TRIP lamp.
brief:
**Client:** Riverside bottling plant (fictional).
**Equipment:** return conveyor **CV-7**, 2.2 kW motor, FLC 4.6 A.

Operators need to run the conveyor backwards to clear jams.

**Scope**
- Reversing contactor pair **KM1** (forward) and **KM2** (reverse), electrically interlocked with NC auxiliaries and mechanically interlocked.
- One overload **F2** after both contactors, TRIP lamp **H1**.
- STOP must be pressed before changing direction.
- No automatic restart.

**Deliverables:** wired and tested starter, interlock proof recorded on the test sheet.

ioList.connection: Parallel with KM1 13-14, then KM2 21-22 to KM1 A1
Parallel with KM2 13-14, then KM1 21-22 to KM2 A1

ioList.type: 3 poles, 13-14 NO, 21-22 NC, 24 V DC coil
3 poles, 13-14 NO, 21-22 NC, 24 V DC coil
ioList.connection: L1 and L3 swapped at its input

logic.condition: S1 pressed, KM2 out, no trip
S2 pressed, KM1 out, no trip

logic.action: Its 21-22 opens: the other cannot pull in

logicNote: This design needs STOP before reversing. If the machine must reverse straight from running, add a delay so the motor stops first, and check the mechanics can take it.

schedule.step: Isolation, lock off and prove dead
Mount contactor pair with mechanical interlock, F2, control gear
Wire power circuit with phase swap on KM2
Wire control circuit with both interlocks
Functional test: directions, interlocks, overload; machine guarded

testIntro: Run the starter and record each result. Start each row from rest: press STOP first.

testSheet.text: Press FORWARD. Running current once up to speed
While running forward, press and hold REVERSE. Is KM2 energised?
While running forward, is KM1 energised?
From rest, press REVERSE. Speed once up to speed
Running in reverse, press TEST on F2. Is H1 lit?

faults.report: The wire from KM2 4 to F2 3 is broken: reverse runs on two phases.
Reverse holding contact KM2 13-14 does not close.
A stray link bridges the FORWARD button: KM1 pulls in as soon as power is on.
STOP button contact 11-12 is open: nothing will start.

faultChecks.fail: KM1 is in before any button is pressed.

extraReports: Nothing is wrong: the starter works as specified.
modelAnswer:
**Test sheet:** forward current about **4.6 A**. Pressing REVERSE while running forward does **not** pull in KM2 (KM1 21-22 is open and has 24 V across it). Reverse speed **1430 rpm**. Overload TEST lights H1 and drops out KM2.

**Interlock proof:** record that each direction blocks the other, and that the mechanical interlock is fitted.

**Fault notes:** if a direction starts but does not hold, measure across that contactor's 13-14 while it is in. If nothing starts at all, work from G1 + along the common path: S0, then F2 95-96.
schematicIntro: The working starter. Run forward and reverse (press STOP between), try REVERSE while running forward, and watch the event log.
